title: Eden
lead: The garden God planted in the east, where the first humans lived with him (Genesis 2–3). Prophets use it as the picture of a restored land (Isaiah 51:3; Ezekiel 36:35), and "paradise" became a name for the life to come (Luke 23:43; Revelation 2:7).

sections.b: After Genesis, Eden is "the garden of the LORD" (Genesis 13:10) and "the garden of God" on "the holy mountain of God" (Ezekiel 28:13–14; 31:8–9). Joel contrasts a land "like the garden of Eden" with the desert left by judgment (Joel 2:3), and Isaiah and Ezekiel promise that ruined Zion will become like Eden (Isaiah 51:3; Ezekiel 36:35). The Septuagint's word for the garden, paradeisos, gave Jewish and Christian writers the word "paradise" for the place of the righteous after death (Luke 23:43; 2 Corinthians 12:4). Revelation 22:1–5 brings back the river and the tree of life in the New Jerusalem. Many scholars see Eden as the first sanctuary, the model for the tabernacle and temple (see the note at Genesis 2:15).
